cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Recognize Me
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And who stopped it leaning into the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

mechanism: A makes permission for a bridge-opening ceremony depend on explicit personal recognition, exercising the authority A wants acknowledged.
confusable: This near-neighbor pair needs both assumed rank and an active attempt to elicit acknowledgment, not just boasting.
comparison: The civic ceremony negotiates public credit before opening; the catering scene turns a practical service request into recognition of expertise.
seedUse: Use D09-a bridge and engineer attribution, with S01 control over permission to begin the ceremony.
